{{Quote|I should be relieved to have survived. Few could say the same. Word trickled down through the grapevine that Birra Seah had been found murdered on some Outer Rim backwater.|Ensign Nanda|<ref name="SW14" />}}
'''Birra Seah''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] who worked as a [[systems designer]] for [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] around [[0 BBY/Legends|0 ABY]]. She was assigned to the construction staff of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], the new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Birra Seah quickly entered in the good graces of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]]' [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|commander-in-chief]], who appointed her acting [[Moff/Legends|Moff]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|This is my assessment and that of other Kuat representatives onsite. The work crews all know of Yavin, and crave the stability that ''only'' the Emperor's attendance could provide.|Birra Seah to Darth Vader|<ref name="SW4:SoY" />}}
Around the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 BBY/Legends|0 ABY]], Birra Seah was an elderly [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] who worked as a [[systems designer]] for the shipbuilding corporation [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]].<ref name="SW4:SoY" /> That company was one of the primary [[Starship/Legends|warship]] supplier for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the authoritarian regime that dominated most of the known [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] at the [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> Seah was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitive]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="SW7">[[Star Wars (2013) 7|''Star Wars'' (2013) 7]]</ref> a mystic energy that flowed through all living things and bound [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] together.<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

Early in 0 ABY, the Empire's weapon of massive destruction known as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] had been [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], a union of freedom-fighting groups opposed to the tyranny of the government. In the wake of that debacle, the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] ordered the construction of a [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] Death Star near the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon]], in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. As a Kuat Drive Yards employee, Birra Seah acted as a liaison between the Empire's [[Imperial High Command/Legends|high command]] and the staff working on the Death Star's construction site.<ref name="SW4:SoY" />

===Rise and a fall===
{{Quote|The Force is strong with you, Birra Seah.''"<br />"''I'm not sure what you mean, My Lord.|Darth Vader and Seah|<ref name="SW4:SoY" />}}
[[File:Birra_Seah_kneels.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Seah kneels before Vader]]
One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], the [[Emperor]] sent his [[Armor/Legends|armored]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|right-hand]], [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] himself, to visit the Death Star working site. The Imperial envoy convened a meeting with the project's [[Supervisor/Legends|supervisors]], which included Seah. The woman, and the assembled [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]] were told that the Emperor was eager to see his [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] completed. [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader menacingly relayed his [[Sith Master/Legends|master's]] discontent with the lack of progress on site. When an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] dared to question the realism of the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg's]] expectations, the Emperor's envoy [[Shiak|stabbed]] him in the back with his [[Color/Legends|crimson]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Seah intervened, asserting that the late officer's claims were true. When Vader asked her who she was and how she dared to back up the dead man's words, Seah introduced herself. She diplomatically pointed out that the Emperor, because of his absence, could not fully realize the numerous details that hindered the progress of the working crews. Impressed by her boldness, Vader commented on how strong the Force was with Seah, thus acknowledging her Force-sensitivity. Seah, however, reacted dismissively to that remark. Subsequently, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] ended the meeting, asking for a private conversation with her.<ref name="SW4:SoY" />

When the two were alone, Seah advised Vader not to turn on the officers and construction workers, suggesting that he should keep his hatred for his true enemies. The woman also asked the Supreme Commander to grant her temporary [[Moff/Legends|Moffship]] so she could supervise the project better and have the Death Star completed on schedule. Seah's request was quickly approved. However, Vader urged her to please Palpatine, adding that if she disappointed the Emperor, she would be doomed a fate from which neither the Dark Lord or even the Force itself could shield her.<ref name="SW5:SoY">[[Star Wars (2013) 5|''Star Wars'' (2013) 5]]</ref>

However, Seah's career as a Moff was short lived. When the Emperor came to visit the Death Star, he was greeted by her since his apprentice had been called away. Palpatine treated Seah with intense disdain, stating that a mere functionary like her did not deserve to be granted Moffship. Humiliated and deeply insulted, Seah was ordered to confine herself to her quarters until Palpatine decided her fate. Feeling hopeless, she attempted to commit [[Death/Legends|suicide]] by pressing a blaster against her chest. However, Seah's self-annihilation attempt was stopped when the disembodied voice of Darth Vader called to her, ordering to retain her arm. Thanks to Seah's Force-sensitivity, she and Vader were able to communicate over a distance by [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]]. The Emperor's right-hand told his protégée that he still had use for her and would protect her from the sovereign's wrath.<ref name="SW7" />

===Spy of the Dark Lord===
{{Quote|You have new orders. Skywalker is to be detained at any and all costs. And then you, Birra Seah, will bring him to me.|Vader, to Seah|<ref name="SW9">[[Star Wars (2013) 9|''Star Wars'' (2013) 9]]</ref>}}
[[File:Seah_suicide.png|thumb|200px|Birra Seah attempts to commit suicide]]
Shortly after, Birra Seah was made a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] and transferred to the [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], a Star Destroyer that had once been the flagship of Vader and was now the command vessel of the young [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Kell Bircher]].<ref name="SW7" /> The Emperor had taken the Devastator away from the Dark Lord as a punishment following the destruction of the Death Star,<ref name="SW 1 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 1|''Star Wars'' (2013) 1]]</ref> and the armored man sought to keep an eye on Bircher.<ref name="SW7" />

Shorlty after Seah's reassignment, the ''Devastator'' captured two couriers suspected of being Rebel collaborators. The two men, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] were actual members of the Rebellion, and Seah informed Vader of their presence.<ref name="SW8">[[Star Wars (2013) 8|''Star Wars'' (2013) 8]]</ref> Suspecting, and rightly so, that Skywalker might be his estranged son, the Supreme Commander charged her with bringing the young man in, assuring her that the Empire would be in her debt.<ref name="SW9" /> However, the two captives escaped custody and kept moving around in the ship, effectively rendering Seah's mission difficult.<ref name="SW10">[[Star Wars (2013) 10|''Star Wars'' (2013) 10]]</ref> Having failed to detain Skywalker, agent Seah ended up abandoning her post. She left the ship aboard an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] after leaving an encrypted message for Vader, extending her apologies for the failed mission and appealing to him for clemency. Upon discovering what she had done, the Dark Lord, however, decreed she would have to die for her defection.<ref name="SW11">[[Star Wars (2013) 11|''Star Wars'' (2013) 11]]</ref> Some time later, word spread that Birra Seah's corpse had been found on a remote planet somewhere in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="SW14" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I understand&hellip; But these men are not your enemy, and neither are the work crews. You have enemies enough.|Birra Seah to Darth Vader|<ref name="SW4:SoY" />}}
[[File:Moff_Seah.png|thumb|left|100px|Acting Moff Birra Seah]]
Around 0 ABY, Seah was an older woman with a slender body shape. Her wrinkled face sported [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] with hooded lids, with a beauty mark on the left side. She had long, black [[Hair/Legends|hair]] with broad white stripes, and she would wear it tightly back to keep her vision clear. Seah also wore high standard [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] and [[Gold/Legends|golden]] jewellery.<ref name="SW4:SoY" /> When she was made acting Moff on the Death Star, Seah took on the [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|regulation uniform]] of the Imperial military, a double-breasted tunic with a matching cap and black [[Boot/Legends|boots]].<ref name="SW5:SoY" /> After being stripped of her Moffship, Seah retained the same type of uniform, although with the appropriate [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank plaque]] for a lieutenant.<ref name="SW7" />

At the beginning, Seah could be at the same time bold and cautious. She did not hesistate to speak her mind in front of Darth Vader, but she did while staying in her place so she would not attract the Dark Lord's anger.<ref name="SW4:SoY" /> That attitude proved rewarding when the demanding Supreme Commander took her in his good graces and agreed to appoint her to Moffship.<ref name="SW5:SoY" /> Seah was also capable of reasoning Vader, helping him understand that he should keep his anger for the Empire's enemies rather than unleash it on those who worked under his orders.<ref name="SW4:SoY" /> However, the way the Emperor treated her before she could even prove herself broke her confidence and drove her to suicidal thoughts.<ref name="SW7" /> As time went by, the missions Vader gave to her put Seah under heavy pressure, and she ended up falling apart completely.<ref name="SW14" />

==Behind the scenes==
Birra Seah first appeared in the [[Star Wars (2013) 4|fourth issue]] of the comic book series titled simply [[Star Wars (2013)|''Star Wars'']] published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]. The issue was written by [[Brian Wood]], illustrated by [[Carlos D'Anda]] and colored by [[Gabe Eltaeb]]. It was released on [[April]] [[April 10|10]] [[2013]].<ref name="SW4:SoY" />

In [[Star Wars (2013) 5|''Star Wars #5'']], Seah appeared as an Imperial Moff for the first time. The rank plaque she wore in that issue, however, does not correspond<ref name="SW5:SoY" /> with the usual pattern of such insignias as established in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The Moff insignia notably worn by [[Merillion Tarko]],<ref name="TFU2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref> [[Boren Tascl]]<ref name="RO">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: The Rebel Opposition]]''</ref> and [[Leonia Tavira]]<ref name="H1">[[Star Wars Handbook 1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|''Star Wars Handbook'' 1: ''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> had a row of six red squares on top of six blue squares. While Seah's rank plaque had the right number of squares, both colors were displayed on each row.<ref name="SW5:SoY" />
